title: How to change the downloads folder in Safari on Mac: General settings steps and fixes
metaTitle: How to Change the Downloads Folder in Safari on Mac
description: How to change the downloads folder in Safari on Mac: open Safari > Settings > General, pick the File download location, and choose where files save.
targetKeyword: how to change the downloads folder in safari on mac
secondaryKeywords: change download location in Safari on Mac
where Safari saves downloads on Mac
Safari ask where to save downloads
intro: To change the downloads folder in Safari on Mac, open Safari > Settings > General and pick a folder from the File download location pop-up menu. After that, Safari saves new downloads to the folder you chose instead of the default Downloads folder.
tldr: Open Safari > Settings > General, then use the File download location pop-up menu.
Choose Other to pick one folder, or choose Ask for each download to pick a folder every time.
Press ⌥⌘L or choose View > Show Downloads to see your recent downloads.
Don't move a file after you download it, or Safari can't find it anymore.
On macOS Tahoe, some users saw Safari ignore a custom folder. A folder inside Documents worked for some of them, but no cause is confirmed.

blocks.text: Where the download setting lives in Safari

The setting sits inside Safari's own Settings window. Open Safari, then choose Safari > Settings from the menu bar. Click General at the top of the window. The option you want is the File download location pop-up menu.

Older guides use a different name. A MacRumors guide from June 2020 says Safari > Preferences, then the General tab. Apple's current guide says Settings. The General tab and the pop-up work the same way in both, so follow whichever name your menu shows.
Safari saves downloads to the Downloads folder in your home folder unless you change it. That is the default. You can return to it at any time, as covered later in this guide.
Pick one folder or ask for each download
The pop-up gives you two paths. The first sends every download to one folder. Choose Other, browse to the folder, and confirm it. From then on, Safari saves new files there without asking.

The second path is Ask for each download. Safari asks where to save a file as each download starts. That suits people who download many kinds of files and want to sort them on the spot. It adds one decision for every file you download.

Here is a worked example. Say you download invoices, photos, and installers in the same week. A single folder called Downloads works if you clear it regularly. Ask for each download works better if you already keep an Invoices folder and a Photos folder and file each item as it arrives.
Choose a folder you can find again

Desktop is the most tempting choice because it is always on screen. It works for a handful of files. A Desktop full of downloads is hard to scan, though, and files pile up fast. A subfolder inside Documents, or a new folder called Inbox, keeps things in order.

Create the folder before you open the pop-up. Give it a name you will recognize later, such as Safari Downloads or Inbox. A name like Untitled Folder makes the Other window harder to read, because you have to open each folder to check what it holds.

items: Pick a folder on a drive you use every day, so you never wonder where it is.
Be careful with folders that sync to a cloud service, since every download then syncs too.
Use one main folder for downloads, not one per project, so you have one place to check.
Write the folder path down if it is new to you, so you can find it in a hurry.

blocks.text: Check where your downloads went

Open the downloads list with View > Show Downloads, or press ⌥⌘L. Each download appears with its file name. Apple's download guide also describes a toolbar button near the top-right corner of the Safari window. That button stays hidden while the list is empty, so you may not see it until your first download finishes.

The General tab has a second list option, Remove download list items. It controls when items drop off the list. Look at it once and set it to suit how you work. It is about the list, not the folder you picked.
Moving files after download breaks Safari's link

Apple's download guide is blunt about this. If you move a file or change the download location after downloading it, Safari can't find the file. The item still sits in the list, but Safari has lost track of where the file is.

Here is how it plays out. You download a contract PDF on Monday. On Tuesday, you drag it from Downloads into a client folder. On Wednesday you click it in the downloads list, and Safari reports that it can't find the file. Open the file in Finder instead, because Finder shows the real location.

Changing the download location also raises a question about old files. Apple's guide does not say whether earlier downloads move to the new folder. Don't assume they will. Check the old folder before you empty it.
Common mistakes with the download folder

items: Looking for the setting somewhere else on the Mac, when it lives inside Safari's Settings window.
Choosing Other, then closing the window before you confirm the folder you want.
Moving a download out of its folder, then clicking it in Safari's list and wondering why it fails.
Expecting old downloads to follow the new setting. Apple's guide does not promise that.
Choosing Desktop for everything, then losing track of work files among personal ones.
Assuming Ask for each download always prompts. One Apple Community user reported it did not.

blocks.text: Safari still saves to Desktop on macOS Tahoe

Some users report that Safari ignored a custom folder and saved to Desktop instead. One Apple Community thread describes a folder named Inbox that Safari did not use on macOS Tahoe. Other people in the thread said the default is Downloads, which matches Apple's guide.

Two workarounds came up in that thread. One user reported that an Inbox folder inside Documents worked. Another said a folder on Desktop worked. Nobody recorded a cause, and the thread closed without an official fix. Treat both as workarounds that helped some people.

If this happens to you, start with the basics. Reopen Settings, check that the pop-up shows your folder, and download a small test file. If the file still lands on Desktop, try a folder inside Documents. A related report in the same thread says the Screen Capture tool ignored the custom folder too.
When Ask for each download does not prompt

A second thread describes the opposite problem. A user chose Ask for each download, but Safari still saved files to the Downloads folder. A volunteer pointed to the File download location pop-up and asked for error details. The thread closed without a recorded fix.

Try these checks before you give up. Confirm the pop-up shows Ask for each download. Quit Safari completely and open it again. Then start a fresh download, not a retry from the list. If the prompt still does not appear, switch to one folder so your files land where you expect.
Go back to the default Downloads folder

To return to the default, open the File download location pop-up, choose Other, and select the Downloads folder in your home folder. MacRumors says Safari saves to Downloads by default, so that is the folder you want. Confirm it, then test with a small download.

Moving the setting back does not move old files, as far as Apple's guide shows. After switching, look in both the old folder and Downloads if a file goes missing. Most lost files turn up in one of those two places.
Which macOS and Safari versions this covers

Apple's current guide for this setting covers macOS 27 and Safari 27. The MacRumors guide names no macOS version at all. The steps match, apart from the older label Preferences. The Tahoe reports come from Apple Community threads, not from Apple's own documentation.

One page I checked calls the macOS 27 version a prerelease, so the setting may look slightly different on your Mac. Check which macOS version your Mac runs before you follow any guide. Then compare the names in the menus with the steps here.
What this guide does not cover

This page covers Safari on the Mac only. The iPhone and iPad have download settings too, but those live in a different place. This page does not give those steps. It also does not cover iCloud Drive or downloads made in other browsers.
Related Safari settings

Once the downloads folder is set, you may want to tidy up the rest of Safari. Other settings have their own guides. Start with [how to change the homepage in Safari](/how-to/change-the-homepage-in-safari) or [how to change the default search engine in Safari](/how-to/change-the-default-search-engine-in-safari).

If you also want to clear old entries from your history, see [how to clear browsing history in Safari](/how-to/clear-browsing-history-in-safari). That guide explains each option and what stays behind after you clear it.
Set the folder once, then check it after updates

Most people set the download folder once and forget it. A quick check after a macOS update is worth the minute it takes. Open the pop-up, confirm your folder is still selected, and download a test file. You will catch a changed setting before a week of files lands in the wrong place.

Keep your folder choice simple. One main folder for all downloads, plus a habit of moving files into project folders on the same day, works for most people. Use Ask for each download only when you like to sort files as you go.

faq.question: Where is the downloads folder setting in Safari on Mac?
faq.answer: Open Safari > Settings > General, then use the File download location pop-up menu. Choose Other to pick a folder, or Ask for each download to choose a folder every time.

faq.question: Does changing the download folder move my old downloads?
faq.answer: Apple's guide does not say whether earlier downloads move to the new folder. Don't assume they do. Check the old folder before you clean it up.

faq.question: Why can't Safari find a file I downloaded?
faq.answer: Apple's download guide says that if you move a file or change the download location after downloading it, Safari can't find the file. Open the file from Finder, or download it again.

faq.question: How do I see recent downloads without opening the folder?
faq.answer: Choose View > Show Downloads, or press ⌥⌘L. The list shows each item by name, whatever folder it was saved to.

faq.question: Why does Safari still save to Desktop on macOS Tahoe?
faq.answer: Some Apple Community users report this. Nobody recorded a cause or an official fix. One user said a folder inside Documents worked, so try that and confirm with a test download.

faq.question: Is Safari > Settings the same as Safari > Preferences?
faq.answer: Apple's current guide uses Settings. An older MacRumors guide from June 2020 uses Preferences. The General tab and the File download location pop-up work the same way in both.

faq.question: Does this work on iPhone or iPad?
faq.answer: No. This guide covers Safari on the Mac only. The iPhone and iPad keep their download settings in a different place, which this page does not cover.

faq.question: Where does Safari save downloads by default?
faq.answer: MacRumors says Safari saves downloads to the Downloads folder by default. You can switch back at any time from the same pop-up menu.

task: Change where Safari saves downloads on a Mac
appliesTo: Safari on Mac, using the Settings window in current macOS
requirements: A folder for downloads, created before you start

steps.name: Open Safari
steps.text: Click the Safari icon in the Dock, or open it from the Applications folder. Make sure Safari is the active app, so its name shows at the left of the menu bar.

steps.name: Open Safari's Settings window
steps.text: In the menu bar, choose Safari > Settings. A separate window opens with tabs across the top. Older guides call this item Preferences, but the window is the same.
steps.tip: If your menu says Preferences, follow the same steps. The tab and pop-up names match.

steps.name: Click the General tab
steps.text: Across the top of the Settings window, click General. The download options sit on this tab, next to other basic settings.

steps.name: Find File download location
steps.text: Look for the File download location pop-up menu. Click it to see your choices. Your current folder, or the Ask option, shows in the pop-up.
steps.tip: Click the pop-up once. Clicking it again closes it without a change.

steps.name: Choose one folder for all downloads
steps.text: Select Other from the pop-up. A Finder window opens. Browse to the folder you want, select it, and confirm. Safari then saves new downloads to that folder.
steps.tip: Create the folder first, so it is ready when the window opens.

steps.name: Or choose Ask for each download
steps.text: Select Ask for each download if you want Safari to ask every time. Safari then asks where to save each file as its download starts.
steps.tip: Use this only if you like to sort files as you go. It adds a step to every download.

steps.name: Test with a small download
steps.text: Download a small file, such as a short PDF from a site you already use. Check the folder you picked. If the file lands there, the setting works. If it lands somewhere else, use the fixes in this guide.

steps.name: Open the downloads list
steps.text: Choose View > Show Downloads, or press ⌥⌘L. Each download appears with its file name. The list is the fastest way to find something you just saved.

troubleshooting.fix: Reopen Settings > General and confirm the pop-up shows your folder. Download a small test file. If it still lands on Desktop, try a folder inside Documents, which one Apple Community user said worked. No cause or official fix is recorded.

troubleshooting.problem: Ask for each download does not prompt
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the pop-up says Ask for each download, then quit Safari and reopen it. Start a fresh download, not a retry from the list. If the prompt still does not appear, choose one folder with Other instead.

troubleshooting.problem: Safari can't find a file I moved
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's guide says moving a file after download breaks Safari's link to it. Find the file in Finder and open it from there, or download it again.

troubleshooting.problem: The downloads list button is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's guide says the toolbar button stays hidden while the list is empty. Start a download, or use View > Show Downloads, or press ⌥⌘L.

troubleshooting.problem: My menu says Preferences, not Settings
troubleshooting.fix: Older guides and some menus use the older name. The General tab and the File download location pop-up work the same way under either name.

troubleshooting.problem: I can't find the default Downloads folder
troubleshooting.fix: Choose Other in the File download location pop-up, then select Downloads in your home folder. MacRumors says Safari saves there by default.
